fields.spec_version: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface) — IEC 62386 multi-part series (originally IEC 60929 Annex E, 1999). TI Application Report SLAA422A 'Digital Addressable Lighting Interface (DALI) Implementation Using MSP430 Value Line Microcontrollers' (November 2009 — Revised October 2012).

lineage.version: Original DALI in IEC 60929 Annex E
lineage.summary: DALI was first defined as Annex E of IEC 60929 'AC supplied electronic ballasts for tubular fluorescent lamps — performance requirements'. The annex specified the 2-wire bus, Manchester encoding at 1200 baud, the YAAAAAAB address byte format, the basic command set, and configuration via INITIALIZE/RANDOMIZE/COMPARE/WITHDRAW addressing iteration.

Bus protocol moved from IEC 60929 Annex E to a dedicated multi-part IEC 62386 series. IEC 62386-101 (system), -102 (control gear, generic protocol), -201 (DT0 fluorescent), -202 (DT1 self-contained emergency), -203 (DT2 discharge), -204 (DT3 low-voltage halogen), -205 (DT4 incandescent), -206 (DT5 0/1-10V converter), -207 (DT6 LED), -208 (DT7 switching) and -209 (DT8 colour control).
TI publishes SLAA422 demonstrating a DALI control gear implementation on the MSP430F2131 microcontroller using the TPS62260LED-338 EVM.

Adds Appendix B 'DALI Implementation With the MSP430G2xx2 Value Line Devices' — re-targets the implementation to the Launchpad MSP-EXP430G2 hardware. Introduces dali_demo_hw.h hardware abstraction (Table 6) so the same DALI core code runs on MSP430F2131 and MSP430G2xx2.

Major revision: -101 General system requirements (replaces IEC 60929 Annex E system clauses), -102 Control gear (generic protocol, now the canonical 'driver' protocol), -103 Control device (new — codifies sensors/buttons/etc as protocol-level peers). DiiA introduces formal certification under the 'DALI-2' brand.
Tunable-white and RGB device-type 8 specifications refined; integrates with the DALI Alliance's certification program.
Parts -301..-305 published for push button (-301), absolute input device (-302), occupancy sensor (-303), light sensor (-304), and timer (-305) control-device types.

related_specifications.name: IEC 60929 Annex E
related_specifications.description: Original DALI bus protocol annex (1999), now superseded by IEC 62386-101 / -102.

related_specifications.name: IEC 62386-101
related_specifications.description: General requirements — System (electrical interface and addressing).

related_specifications.name: IEC 62386-102
related_specifications.description: General requirements — Control gear (the generic 'driver' protocol). Mandatory for every DALI driver.

related_specifications.name: IEC 62386-103
related_specifications.description: General requirements — Control device. Defines the protocol-level peer for application controllers (DALI 2 era).

related_specifications.description: Device-type-specific control-gear parts (DT0..DT8 — fluorescent / emergency / discharge / halogen / incandescent / 0-10V / LED / switching / colour control).

related_specifications.name: IEC 62386-301..-305
related_specifications.description: Device-type-specific control-device parts (push button / absolute input / occupancy / light sensor / timer).

backward_compat_traps.B_eq_0: Data byte is arc-power level 0..254 (255 = MASK).
backward_compat_traps.B_eq_1: Data byte is indirect command code (0x00..0xFF).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Decoder must check B BEFORE interpreting the data byte; treating every frame as 'indirect' breaks 90% of normal traffic.

backward_compat_traps.1100xxx1: Special command range ENABLE DEVICE TYPE / DTR1 / DTR2 / WRITE MEMORY LOCATION.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Pattern overlaps with Y=1 group addressing (1AAAAAAB); must use the explicit address-byte table to disambiguate special commands.

backward_compat_traps.level_255: MASK — do NOT change Actual Level.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Level 255 is not 'full' — it is the magic 'leave alone' value used by stored scenes and other mechanisms.

backward_compat_traps.rejected_frame: Manchester error / out-of-window / unsupported command → silently discarded.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Control device cannot distinguish 'gear absent' from 'gear ignored command' without an explicit follow-up QUERY.

backward_compat_traps.destructive: RESET 0x20, STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS 0x80, STORE DTR AS MAX/MIN/.. 0x2A..0x2F, STORE DTR AS SCENE n 0x40..0x4F.
backward_compat_traps.rule: Must be sent twice within 100 ms to commit.
backward_compat_traps.trap: A single send is silently ignored; control device implementations that forget the second send appear to fail at random.
Outside the window the response is invalid; control devices that sample too early miss it, too late confuse it with the next forward frame.
Bursty traffic at < 22×TE inter-frame is dropped on the wire; many implementations use the recommended 13.5 ms to absorb timer jitter.

backward_compat_traps.ti_references: IEC 62383-102 / -107 in the SLAA422A references list.
backward_compat_traps.correct: IEC 62386-102 / -107 (DALI). 62383 is an LED measurement standard (Lighting equipment - flicker / stroboscopic). The TI report's reference list contains the typo.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Minimum Level shall not be set below PHYS_MIN_LEVEL.
backward_compat_traps.ti_example: PHYS_MIN_LEVEL = 90 (≈ 1.17% PWM duty for red/green LEDs at 1.6 kHz).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Software sets of Minimum Level below PHYS_MIN_LEVEL must be silently clamped.

backward_compat_traps.missing_features: Commands 129 (Enable Write Memory), 275 (WRITE MEMORY LOCATION), 224..227 (Reference System Power / Enable/Disable Current Protector / Select Dimming Curve), 242..251 (LED Open/Short/Change in Load/Thermal etc).
backward_compat_traps.trap: SLAA422A control gear silently ignores these; control device must check QUERY EXTENDED VERSION NUMBER 240 to confirm support.

fields.version_naming_history_note: DALI was first published as IEC 60929 Annex E in 1999. The dedicated IEC 62386 series replaced the annex in 2009 (parts 101, 102, 201, 207 etc), and the 2014 'DALI 2' revision added IEC 62386-103 for control devices plus formal certification by the DALI Alliance (formerly Activity Group DALI of LightingEurope, then DiiA). The TI SLAA422A application report uses the 2009-vintage IEC 62386 semantics and references the older IEC 62383-102 / -107 numbering in its bibliography (likely typo for 62386). The DALI Alliance maintains the modern command set + certification at https://www.dali-alliance.org/.
